root_cause: The inner relay-fetch `try` block in DevicesTab's device-load effect ended in a bare `catch {}` that discarded the error. On a relay failure the slotMap silently fell back to local-only key packages and the UI rendered with no signal, so the user could believe an incomplete device list was complete (relay-only devices, e.g. siblings not in local IDB, would be missing).
fix_description: Extracted the device-load logic into a pure, testable helper (src/components/DevicesTab.loadDevices.ts) that returns { entries, relayFetchError }. The formerly-bare catch now sets relayFetchError = true (still non-fatal: local devices are still returned). DevicesTab consumes the flag into a new `relayFetchError` state and renders a visible warning ('Could not reach relay — device list may be incomplete.') using the project's existing inline `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` error-box pattern (same as actionError), placed at the top of the device list. The cancelled-effect guard already in place prevents setState after unmount. No toast library was added; the non-fatal policy is unchanged.
files_changed: src/components/DevicesTab.tsx — added relayFetchError state; replaced the inlined load logic (incl. the bug's bare catch) with a call to loadDevices(); removed the now-duplicated DeviceEntry type and extractSlot helper (moved into the new module); render the relay-fetch warning via the existing inline destructive error-box pattern.
src/components/DevicesTab.loadDevices.ts (new) — pure load helper holding the extracted slot-mapping + relay-fetch logic; the relay catch now reports a relayFetchError flag instead of swallowing.
tests_added: loadDevices flags relayFetchError when the relay request rejects (the reproduction test — fails against the old silent bare-catch with 'expected false to be true', passes with the fix; also asserts local devices still render).
loadDevices does not flag relayFetchError on a successful relay fetch (and unions remote slots).
loadDevices does not flag relayFetchError when there are no relays to query.

verification_questions.does_the_reproduction_test_fail_without_: Yes. With the catch reverted to the old silent bare-catch (no flag set), the reproduction test fails with AssertionError: expected false to be true on relayFetchError, while the success-path and no-relays tests still pass — confirming the test isolates the bug, not a syntax/assertion error.
verification_questions.does_the_fix_make_the_reproduction_test_: Yes. After restoring the flag, all 3 new tests pass and the full suite is 283/283.
verification_questions.is_the_failure_now_user_visible: Yes. A relay-fetch failure sets relayFetchError state, rendered as an inline destructive warning box (data-testid='device-relay-error') above the device list. The message tells the user the list may be incomplete.
verification_questions.is_the_non_fatal_policy_preserved: Yes. loadDevices still returns the locally-known devices on relay failure; the component still renders them. Only an additional warning is shown. A fatal (outer) load error still uses the existing full-pane loadError path, distinct from the relay warning.
verification_questions.any_regressions: No. Unit suite 280→283 (only the 3 new tests added), typecheck clean, make test (build + static export) exits 0.
verification_questions.scope_adherence: No toast library added; no jsdom/RTL component-stack added (matched the repo's pure-logic node/vitest test idiom via extraction); IdentityPanel.tsx:198 left unchanged (see observation).

out_of_scope_observation.finding: IdentityPanel has the identical bare `catch {}` pattern when loading sibling slots from the relay — on relay failure it silently degrades to current-device-only info with no user-visible warning. Same class of bug as this one. NOT fixed here (out of scope for this bug report). A follow-up backlog finding is warranted if the product wants relay-fetch failures surfaced consistently across Settings panels.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The brief assumed a component-level unit test of DevicesTab, but the repo has NO component-rendering test stack — vitest runs in the node environment with no jsdom/happy-dom and no @testing-library/react; all existing unit tests are pure-logic .test.ts. The load logic was also inlined inside a useEffect, untestable in isolation. Resolution: extract the load logic into a pure helper and unit-test the error path there — matched the repo idiom but a slightly larger surface (a new module) than 'add a useState + set it in the catch' implied.
